title: Identify the two blood compartments in a term villus

regions.label: Villous trophoblast surface
regions.observation: An intensely purple rim follows the outside of the villous profile.
regions.interpretation: The trophoblast covering separates the outer maternal blood space from the villous core. The outer syncytial compartment is multinucleated; a visible nucleus is not automatically a separate cell.
regions.limit: This view does not identify every individual trophoblast cell or resolve each plasma membrane.

regions.label: Fetal capillary compartment
regions.observation: Pink erythrocytes occupy an enclosed space within the villous tissue.
regions.interpretation: This internal vascular lumen belongs to the fetal circuit. An endothelial wall and intervening villous tissue separate its erythrocytes from the maternal compartment outside.
regions.limit: Use the enclosing architecture; red staining alone does not identify a blood circuit.

regions.label: Villous stromal core
regions.observation: A paler heterogeneous compartment surrounds internal vessels beneath the outer covering.
regions.interpretation: Villous connective tissue supports internal vessels beneath the trophoblast surface. A thinner local route between a capillary and the surface can shorten the distance available for exchange.
regions.limit: H&E alone does not confidently assign every stromal nucleus a lineage.

regions.label: Intervillous compartment
regions.observation: Pink erythrocytes occur outside the villous covering, toward the left of the field.
regions.interpretation: These erythrocytes lie outside the villous surface, in the maternal compartment described by the source.
regions.limit: One field does not show the supplying spiral artery or maternal venous drainage.

regions.label: Peripheral syncytial nuclear aggregate
regions.observation: Closely packed purple nuclei cluster near the upper-right surface.
regions.interpretation: These clustered surface nuclei are associated with the shared syncytial compartment. Nuclear number and arrangement must not be mistaken for a count of individual trophoblast cells.
regions.limit: A surface nuclear aggregate alone does not establish disease or a molecular subtype.

model: I see a trophoblast-covered villous profile with internal erythrocyte-containing capillaries and a separate outer space containing erythrocytes. These relationships distinguish fetal capillary blood from maternal intervillous blood. I need a calibrated scale and wider section context before measuring structures or describing the whole placenta. The surface nuclear aggregate alone does not establish a diagnosis.
